error.signature: AI tells a tourist they can buy a South African SIM card and use it immediately with no registration

verdict.summary: South African law (RICA, Act 70 of 2002) bars mobile operators from activating any SIM card until the buyer's identity and address are registered; a passport alone is not enough because proof of address is also required, though airport and flagship network stores routinely accept an accommodation booking confirmation as that proof for tourists.

dead_ends.action: Buy a prepaid SIM card and expect it to work for calls or data immediately, without providing ID or an address document
dead_ends.why_fails: RICA (Regulation of Interception of Communications and Provision of Communication-related Information Act 70 of 2002) prohibits an electronic communications service provider from activating a SIM card or allowing its use until the registration requirements are met; an unregistered SIM cannot be switched on, and networks such as Vodacom state registration can take up to 24 hours outside of dedicated in-store processing.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Travelers assume a passport alone is sufficient identification, but proof of address is a separate, mandatory part of RICA registration that a passport does not satisfy on its own.

workarounds.action: Bring your passport plus a hotel/Airbnb booking confirmation showing your name and the accommodation's address, and register at an airport or flagship network store
workarounds.how: Vodacom and MTN accept a passport for identity, and in practice their airport and flagship stores are set up to accept a printed or digital accommodation booking confirmation as proof of address for foreign tourists who have no South African utility bill.
